text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: SEV=2 page fired -> service: inference-frontend-prod. Alert: HTTP 5xx rate spike on /v1/generate in prod-us-west-2. Error rate = 12% over 5m (threshold 5%). Pager: on-call CARLA.
carla_oncall: ack. I'm on it. paging @bob_sre as backup.
bob_sre: ack. in transit, will grab logs, redis stats, and GPU telemetry.
alice_dev: looking at app logs — a lot of "kv-cache miss" and repeated "tensor alloc failed" around 14:05 UTC; opening a short trace.
alice_dev: snippet:
```
[14:05:58] ERROR model-serving: failed to run forward: CUDA OOM while allocating tensor (size=1.2GB)
[14:06:02] WARN router: request dropped, fallback not configured
```
dave_support: customers reporting timeouts and 502s on /v1/generate, a few enterprise tenants on us-west affected. Most requests succeed, but spike concentrated on long-context jobs.
carla_oncall: quick mitigation options: 1) scale replicas in us-west canary pool; 2) enable fallback to smaller model variant (model-small-v2); 3) throttle long requests via ingress. Which is fastest?
bob_sre: start with fallback + scale. I'll trigger HPA/replica bump and set routing override. Alice, can you smoke test model-small-v2?
alice_dev: running smoke now. health ok, short generation looks fine. ok to route 30% traffic to fallback.
bob_sre: executing commands now:
```
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/model-serving --replicas=10
redwoodctl route override set --service inference --region us-west-2 --policy fallback=model-small-v2 --weight 30
```
carla_oncall: applied scale and route override. Monitoring: error rate dropping from 12% -> 6% in ~3m.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: page acknowledged by carla_oncall; escalated to bob_sre. Silence window applied for same alert group.
ellen_pm: heads-up: should we notify affected enterprise customers? dave, coordinate comms.
dave_support: pinged account teams, sent status note to SRE updates channel, and messaged two affected customers directly. No full outage declared.
alice_dev: logs still show CUDA memory pressure on some hosts; starting a node drain to move pods off a suspect GPU node.
bob_sre: cordoning & draining node ip-10-0-23-7, evicting pods, verifying restarts.
carla_oncall: error-rate now 2.2% over 5m. Latency slightly up but within SLO. Scaling down route override to 10%, will remove if stable.
carla_oncall: final mitigation steps: scale down to stable replicas=6 and remove override.
```
redwoodctl route override remove --service inference --region us-west-2
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/model-serving --replicas=6
```
carla_oncall: post-incident action items: - root cause hypothesis: opportunistic CUDA OOM due to memory fragmentation + concurrent long-context requests; - short-term: add request length rejection >20k tokens; - medium-term: reserve autoscale headroom + smarter bin-packing; - long-term: automated fallback routing when OOM signature detected.
bob_sre: creating incident ticket INC-17724 with timeline, logs, and GPU telemetry. Assigning to eng-runtime + eng-ml. Will attach graphs.
ellen_pm: please include customer impact summary for comms; dave_support to own notifications.
dave_support: will prepare customer-facing timeline and request SLO credit review for affected accounts.
carla_oncall: handing off monitoring to @bob_sre for overnight watch. bob, you're on-call until 02:00 UTC.
bob_sre: ack handoff. I will monitor dashboards and escalate if error rate >5% or CUDA OOMs recur.
carla_oncall: thanks team :thumbsup: :rotating_light: closing live thread. Postmortem and logs linked here: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-17724 and runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/http-5xx
